name: Shecaniah
overview: Shecaniah was a male Levite priest, specifically noted as the tenth-chosen priest among the twenty-four priestly courses established for temple service. He belonged to the line of Ithamar, one of Aaron's sons, which distinguished his priestly lineage. His role reflects a structured and divinely ordained priesthood within ancient Israel's worship system.
namesAndTitles: The name Shecaniah means 'YHWH has taken up his abode,' highlighting a theological emphasis on God's presence dwelling among His people. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 24:11 and was not given directly by God but reflects a meaningful attribute.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Shecaniah as a descendant of Ithamar, linking him to a specific priestly family line. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are recorded in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Shecaniah's significance lies in his role as the tenth priestly leader in the established twenty-four courses, which organized the Levitical priesthood for temple duties. His inclusion in the line of Ithamar underscores the continuation of Aaron's priestly heritage through this branch. This structured division of priests was essential for maintaining orderly worship and service in the temple, reflecting God's design for His covenant community.
